chapter: Art Hodes, Bechet and Blue Note
title: Unrecalled 1945-47 broadcasts with Bechet and others
summary: Welburn asks about Boston and New York broadcasts; Moore does not recall them.

bands.name: Sidney Bechet and His New Orleans Rhythm Kings

blocks.x: Well, you made a number of other recordings with Bechet. There's also what seems to me here a broadcast, an aircheck, which was put out, recorded in May and June of 1945 at the Savoy Cafe in Boston. There weren't any tunes listed. But it's Sidney Bechet and His New Orleans Rhythm Kings. That's the way apparently it's billed. Pops Foster is playing, the piano player is Hank Duncan, and apparently they're not sure whether the drummer is you or a fellow by the name of George Thompson. Do you remember playing Boston with Sidney Bechet.
Let's see...
Bunk Johnson was supposed to have been on trumpet. This is 1945.
No, I wasn't in that band.
Okay. Well, that solves that. Because they had Johnny Wertherst(?), Hank Duncan, Peter Bocage...
Johnny Wertherst(?) was a trumpet player.
That's right. And Peter Bocage, he was in that band. Okay, so you weren't involved in that.
No.
Moore (III) - 44

Now, there was another broadcast that's been put out apparently on the label called Kings Of Jazz. It was recorded in New York here on the 24th of May, 1947. It's got Sidney Bechet, Wild Bill Davidson, George Brunis on trombone and apparently singing, Albert Nicholas on clarinet, James P. Johnson is on piano, Danny Barker is playing the banjo, Pops Foster, and then yourself. The three selections that are on this release include "Wildcat Blues," "Ain't Misbehavin'" and "Blue Turning Gray Over You." Do you remember making a date that included Bechet and James P. Johnson? Some pretty fast company there. This is 1947.
Maybe so, but I don't remember. I don't remember what the (?) at that time...
At that time. George Brunis was the trombone player.
Brunis?
Yeah. He was from the Brunis family. There are several musicians...
Right.
They're out of New Orleans.
I don't remember working in that band. Maaybe I did. Was that at the Savoy?
No, this was in New York.
Moore (III) - 45
New York.
In New York in 1947. We don't have the record at the Institute of Jazz Studies. It's a broadcast, and it's on the Kings of Jazz label. I'll see if I can...
That wasn't with Rudi Blesh, was it?
No, those were later.
Oh, really?
Yeah, those were later. This is apparently 1947. Not apparently, it is 1947. I'll see if I can track it down for you.
